subject: Model multiple latent variables based on recoded items

messages.author: 002e2da732244d04
messages.subject: Model multiple latent variables based on recoded items
parts:
Hello Phil and everyone,

I am currently working on my Master's thesis and were trying to implement Wetzel & Carstensen's (2013) idea using the mirt package, in order to purge data from the effect of response styles:

Specifically, I would like to test a multidimensional PCM (or nominal model) on 9 items. I want to use the original rating scores (from 1 to 5) and an alternative coding of the same items (e.g., 1 0 0 0 0 or 2 1 0 0 0).

If I specify that the first latent variable, F1, be modelled using the first 9 columns of the data matrix (the original ratings) and the second latent variable be modelled based on the next 9 columns, then the package computes a latent variable F1 for/from columns/items 1 to 9 with zero loadings for F2, and a latent variable, F2, based on columns 10 to 18 with zero loadings on F1, that is, as if columns 10 to 18 were separate items, which is not what I need:

model=mirt.model('F1=1-9
                            F2=10-18')

Instead, I want mirt to treat columns 10 to 18 as the same items as 1 to 9 and produce a factor loadings matrix in which only items 1 to 9 are present, with loadings on both factors.

The authors implement this (in another software, ConQuest) by specifying a w matrix indicator variable, that tells kind of "redirects" the equation to the intended columns/values.


I also tried to specify a custom model using the following syntax:

w=rbind(c(1,0),
        c(0,1))

P.Wetzel <- function(par,Theta,ncat){
  dk <- par[1:ncat]
  z <- matrix(0, nrow(Theta), ncat)
  for(i in 1:ncat) z[,i] <- w[1,1]*Theta+w[1,2]*Theta+w[2,1]*Theta+w[2,2]*Theta+dk[i]
  P <- exp(z) / rowSums(exp(z))
  P
}

W <- createItem(name='Wetzel',
                  par=c(dk=c(0,1,1,1,1)),
                  est=c(FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE),
                  P=P.Wetzel)

m=mirt(X,W,itemtype='Wetzel',customItems=list(Wetzel=mod),GenRandomPars=TRUE)

However, I have no idea how to link w to the columns of my data matrix X.

Any thoughts on possible solutions?

Great thanks in advance!

Kristian

parts: Hi Kristian,

On Wed, Feb 25, 2015 at 6:36 AM, Kristian Hristov <kristian....@gmail.com> wrote:

I am currently working on my Master's thesis and were trying to implement Wetzel & Carstensen's (2013) idea using the mirt package, in order to purge data from the effect of response styles:

Specifically, I would like to test a multidimensional PCM (or nominal model) on 9 items. I want to use the original rating scores (from 1 to 5) and an alternative coding of the same items (e.g., 1 0 0 0 0 or 2 1 0 0 0).

That model looks kind of convoluted with all the subscripts, what exactly is going on here? Also, it looks to be suitable for dichotomous items only, with the 1 + term in the denominator (usually, polytomous models have a sum over all possible categories to be in the 'divide by total' family). Perhaps attaching the original paper would help clarify what's going on.

If I specify that the first latent variable, F1, be modelled using the first 9 columns of the data matrix (the original ratings) and the second latent variable be modelled based on the next 9 columns, then the package computes a latent variable F1 for/from columns/items 1 to 9 with zero loadings for F2, and a latent variable, F2, based on columns 10 to 18 with zero loadings on F1, that is, as if columns 10 to 18 were separate items, which is not what I need:

Instead, I want mirt to treat columns 10 to 18 as the same items as 1 to 9 and produce a factor loadings matrix in which only items 1 to 9 are present, with loadings on both factors.

I don't think this is quite right, your model above only had 1 latent trait, whereas this would be estimated with two. It also looks to be very Rasch based, in that no slope parameters per item are estimated (all fixed to 1, and therefore drop out of the equations).

The authors implement this (in another software, ConQuest) by specifying a w matrix indicator variable, that tells kind of "redirects" the equation to the intended columns/values.


I also tried to specify a custom model using the following syntax:

w=rbind(c(1,0),
        c(0,1))

P.Wetzel <- function(par,Theta,ncat){
  dk <- par[1:ncat]
  z <- matrix(0, nrow(Theta), ncat)
  for(i in 1:ncat) z[,i] <- w[1,1]*Theta+w[1,2]*Theta+w[2,1]*Theta+w[2,2]*Theta+dk[i]
  P <- exp(z) / rowSums(exp(z))
  P
}

W <- createItem(name='Wetzel',
                  par=c(dk=c(0,1,1,1,1)),
                  est=c(FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE),
                  P=P.Wetzel)

m=mirt(X,W,itemtype='Wetzel',customItems=list(Wetzel=mod),GenRandomPars=TRUE)

However, I have no idea how to link w to the columns of my data matrix X.

Any thoughts on possible solutions?

I think this is possible to do in mirt with a bit of work, but you may want to look into the TAM package first as it is much more Rasch oriented and has a similar flavour to ConQuest. Alexander (the maintainer) is another great R package developer who actively develops IRT modeling software. Once you get it working there, I'd be happy to help figure out how the same model can be run in mirt, with something a bit more palpable/with reasonable results (I'm sure mirt can, but the equation just looks to confusing to me at the moment). Cheers.

Phil

Great thanks in advance!

Kristian

parts:
Hi Phil,

thank you for the quick reply!

Yes, I do realize my post was a little chaotic/unspecific, so here are some additional details (I also attached the dissertation paper, the relevant article starting at page 136).

I guess the model described in the paper is Rasch-based, but I would like to include item discrimination parameters in my application of it, which explains why the formula in my syntax was for a divide-by-total model. Interestingly, the authors do call their model a multidimensional PCM.

The formula is confusing for me as well, but the sum term with q = 1 to s basically means that there are e.g. 2 dimensions. The first one would for example be the trait of interest, whereas the second is the response style that is modelled using the re-coded items. So we have w1 x Theta1 + w2 + Theta2 - d.

Does that help clarify the issue? I'll take a look at TAM in the meantime, thanks for the idea!


I actually have another question as well, which relates to the formula used in the createItem syntax:
So, I managed to define a unidimensional GPCM that gives (nearly) the same output as using pcmRauto <- mirt(X, 1, 'gpcm'):

name <- 'GPC'
par <- c(ak=c(0,1,2,3,4),a=1,d=c(0,1,1,1,1))
est <- c(FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE, TRUE, FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE)
P.gpc <- function(par, Theta, ncat){
  ak <- par[1:5]
  a  <- par[6]
  d  <- par[7:11]

z <- matrix(0, nrow(Theta), ncat)
  for(i in 1:ncat)
z[,i] <- ak[i]*a*Theta + d[i]

P <- exp(z) / rowSums(exp(z))
  P
}

pcm1 <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.gpc)
pcmR <- mirt(X, 1, 'pcm1', customItems=list(pcm1=pcm1))

However, I have no idea how to extend it to a multidimensional model. Using the following syntax outputs the same d values, but different a parameters as pcmRauto <- mirt(X, 2, 'gpcm'):

P.gpc2 <- function(par, Theta, ncat){
  ak <- par[1:5]
  a1  <- par[6]
  a2  <- par[7]
  d  <- par[8:12]

z <- matrix(0, nrow(Theta), ncat)
  for(i in 1:ncat)
z[,i] <- ak[i]*a1*Theta[,1] + ak[i]*a2*Theta[,2] + d[i]

P <- exp(z) / rowSums(exp(z))
  P
}

pcm2 <- createItem(name='GPC2',
                  par=c(ak=c(0,1,2,3,4),a1=1,a2=1,d=c(0,1,1,1,1)),
                  est=c(FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE, TRUE,TRUE, FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE),
                  P=P.gpc2)
pcm2R <- mirt(X, 2, 'pcm2', customItems=list(pcm2=pcm2))

How should I do that? Basically, after solving that issue, I only need to find a way to implement that w index variable.

Best,
Kristian

These both basically just look like the itemtype = 'gpcm' in mirt, so there isn't much fancy going on. The difference to accomplish your goal is in the second item type, where the ak values are different for each trait (but obviously have the same length). I shorthand this internally for quicker computations, but extending it to be unequal for both traits should be possible (and indeed quite interesting). 

This does seems like something TAM could handle at the moment though, at least in the Rasch ase, so hopefully you'll have some luck there. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Model multiple latent variables based on recoded items
parts:
I've made some strides on this in the development version on Github, which you are welcome to check out. Using the new gpcm_mats input, you can specify a list of scoring coefficients for each dimension in each item, so that should accomplish your goal. E.g., setting up an extreme negative response style for trait 2 but with a gpcm scoring in trait 1 could be done like so:

```
library(mirt)
mats <- list()
mats[1:20] <- list(matrix(c(0:4, 1,0,0,0,0), 5))
a <- matrix(c(rep(1, 10), numeric(20), rep(1, 10)), 20)
d <- cbind(0, matrix(rnorm(4*20), 20))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, 'gpcm', gpcm_mats = mats)

model <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-10
                    F2 = 11-20
                    COV = F1*F2')

#standard partial credit
gpcm <- mirt(dat, model, 'gpcm') 
coef(gpcm, simplify=TRUE) #coefs way off

# customized scoring matrix
gpcm_custom <- mirt(dat, model, 'gpcm', gpcm_mats = mats)
coef(gpcm_custom, simplify=TRUE) #coefs recovered here

anova(gpcm, gpcm_custom) #information alone, gpcm_custom look better
M2(gpcm)
M2(gpcm_custom)
```

Let me know if you have any questions. Cheers.

Phil

par <- c(ak=c(0,1,2,3,4),a=1,d=c(0,1,1,1,1))
est <- c(FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE, TRUE, FALSE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE,TRUE)
P.gpc <- function(par, Theta, ncat){
  ak <- par[1:5]
  a  <- par[6]
  d  <- par[7:11]
  z <- matrix(0, nrow(Theta), ncat)
  for(i in 1:ncat)
    z[,i] <- ak[i]*a*Theta + d[i]
  P <- exp(z) / rowSums(exp(z))
  P
}
pcm1 <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.gpc)
pcmR <- mirt(X, 1, 'pcm1', customItems=list(pcm1=pcm1))

However, I have no idea how to extend it to a multidimensional model. Using the following syntax outputs the same d values, but different a parameters as pcmRauto <- mirt(X, 2, 'gpcm'):

  a2  <- par[7]

                  P=P.gpc2)

How should I do that? Basically, after solving that issue, I only need to find a way to implement that w index variable.

The difference to accomplish your goal is in the second item type, where the ak values are different for each trait (but obviously have the same length). I shorthand this internally for quicker computations, but extending it to be unequal for both traits should be possible (and indeed quite interesting). 

This does seems like something TAM could handle at the moment though, at least in the Rasch ase, so hopefully you'll have some luck there. Cheers.

Phil
 

Best,
